task: Phase 3, slice A. Generalise the Restaurant's robot-only paper customer into ONE shared paper-character adapter plus ONE shared casting helper, both usable by any minigame, and let all five saved Coloring subjects visit the Restaurant instead of only the robot.
context: IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE PLAN THIS COMES FROM: there are no paper ANIMALS. Penguin, chicken, cat and dog were authored last pass, rejected on sight and removed. The registry holds exactly five subjects - robot, snowman, gingerbread, hero, ninja - and all five are humanoid. Nothing here should reference paper animals or a Zoo animal integration; neither exists.

src/minigames/restaurant/robotCustomer.js is the shipped, working adapter for exactly one subject. It wraps a fresh paper puppet in a THREE.Group carrying playAnimation / updateAnimation / disposeCharacter - the same duck type src/systems/characters.js create() returns - and holds a rendered yaw EDGE_GUARD = 0.44 rad clear of +-PI/2 so the flat sheet never becomes invisible. That yaw logic is proven (the sheet never drops below 42.6% of its width, verified by sweep) and must be preserved exactly, not reinvented.

src/minigames/restaurant/robotCasting.js is the shipped casting logic: a guaranteed slot reserved uniformly from the first three arrivals plus EXTRA_ROBOT_CHANCE = 0.25 for every other slot, and pickRobotRecord avoiding an immediate repeat.

src/minigames/restaurant/index.js already reads per-customer presentation from the character object: customer.groundY, customer.seatedY, customer.bubbleOffsetY and customer.dialogueOffsetY, plus character.hitTargetY and character.hitTargetScale for the click box. Those seams exist and must keep working - do not add new ones and do not put subject names in index.js.

coloringSession.js exports savedCreations() (all records, each { subjectId, artwork, crowd }) and savedRobots() (the robot-only compatibility view). Records are read-only and must never be consumed or mutated.
Subjects live in src/minigames/coloring/subjects/*.js and are deeply frozen. They currently carry liveScale but no cross-game metadata.
A second slice will add paper VISITORS to the Zoo against whatever this slice freezes, so the adapter and the casting helper must be genuinely game-neutral, not Restaurant-shaped.
requirements: NEW src/systems/paperCharacter.js - the one paper-character adapter, shared by every minigame. Export createPaperCharacter({ subject, artwork, textureSize, presentation }) returning a THREE.Group with playAnimation(name, options), updateAnimation(dt) and disposeCharacter(), plus the presentation values the host reads off the character. Move the yaw guard, the eased rendered yaw and EDGE_GUARD across UNCHANGED in behaviour.

ANIMATION MAPPING stays name-based and generic: 'walk' -> the subject's hop, 'idle' -> idle, 'emote-yes' -> celebrate then back to idle, 'static' -> idle with the clock held, anything else -> idle. Personality comes from the subject, so a snowman wobbles and a ninja crouches with no per-subject code in the adapter.

NEW cross-game subject metadata on every subject: crossGame: { restaurantCustomer: true, zooVisitor: true } for all five. Eligibility must be read from this, never inferred from category - a later subject may be a character and still not belong in a restaurant.

NEW per-subject presentation metadata so index.js keeps no magic numbers: presentation: { restaurant: { scale, groundY, seatedY, bubbleOffsetY, dialogueOffsetY, hitTargetY, hitTargetScale } }. Derive each subject's numbers the way the robot's were derived - the robot's scale comes from matching a 0.72-scaled human's height (characters.js TARGET_HEIGHT 1.95), not from a typed constant - and keep the robot's shipped values identical so nothing about the robot changes. A taller or shorter silhouette must sit at the table without sinking, floating or clipping.

NEW src/systems/creationCasting.js - the one casting helper, pure, no three.js, seedable. Export something equivalent to chooseCreationSlots({ slots, eligibleCount, guaranteed = 1, earlyWindow = 3, extraChance = 0.25, random }) returning which slot indices are paper, and pickCreation({ records, random, used, lastIndex }) which prefers a record not yet used this session before repeating one and never returns lastIndex twice running. The guarantee must be an explicitly reserved slot, never a probability roll, and must be impossible to lose to randomness. With eligibleCount 0 nothing is ever paper.

The Restaurant uses the shared helper and the shared adapter, and draws from savedCreations() filtered by crossGame.restaurantCustomer - so all five subjects may now visit, not just the robot. Behaviour with zero eligible creations must be byte-for-byte the all-human Restaurant of today.

DELETE src/minigames/restaurant/robotCustomer.js and src/minigames/restaurant/robotCasting.js once their behaviour lives in the shared modules, and move or rewrite their tests to cover the shared modules instead. Do not leave five adapters, two casting helpers, or a robot special case behind.
savedRobots() may now be unused. If nothing imports it, remove it and its test; if something still does, leave it. Do not keep a dead compatibility view for its own sake.
Each cross-game appearance builds a FRESH puppet from the saved artwork and disposes it on exit. Saved records are never consumed, mutated or reordered.
constraints: Do NOT touch the Zoo in this slice. It is the next one.

Do NOT fork Restaurant gameplay. The customer state machine, orders, patience, rival claims, serving and scoring are untouched; the only thing that differs about a paper customer is what customer.character is. There is already a test asserting the state machine has no robot branch - it must keep passing, and it should now assert no subject branch of any kind.
Do not change food preference, and do not let the subject or the child's favourite colour influence it.
Do not billboard a paper customer at the camera. Brief edge-on turning is intentional and wanted; the guard exists only so the sheet never disappears.
Do not change the robot's appearance, scale, seating, bubbles or motion in any way. It is shipped and the owner has seen it.

Do not change the shared paper asset lifecycle logic in paperPuppet.js - the live-puppet count already makes disposal safe across minigames. Verify it covers a Restaurant puppet and say so; do not rewrite it.
Restaurant must not import coloring/index.js. Low-level modules only.
Edit files with your structured patch/edit tool. If a shell-based edit fails once because of quoting or escaping, switch to the structured mechanism - do not try another escaped variant.

Append a dated DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entry: one shared paper-character adapter rather than one per game, cross-game eligibility as subject metadata rather than an inferred category, and presentation metadata per subject rather than numbers in index.js - each with what, why and the rejected alternative.
startingPoints: src/systems/characters.js (TARGET_HEIGHT, and the character duck type to match)
tests: creationCasting: zero eligible creations means no paper slot ever, under every seed; one eligible means the reserved slot is always paper and a whole session can never come out all-human; the reserved slot falls in the early window but is not always slot 0 across seeds; the extra chance is exercised independently; humans stay the majority over many seeded sessions.
pickCreation prefers an unused record before repeating one, never returns the same record twice running when alternatives exist, and never mutates or consumes the record list.

paperCharacter: the adapter exposes position, rotation, scale, visible, add, getWorldPosition, playAnimation, updateAnimation and disposeCharacter for EVERY one of the five subjects; the animation mapping holds; replaying the current name does not restart the cycle; the rendered yaw never sits within EDGE_GUARD of +-PI/2 while rotation.y sweeps a full turn, for every subject; disposeCharacter frees the puppet's own textures and materials but not the shared quad; the saved artwork is never mutated.
Every subject carries crossGame and a restaurant presentation block, and the robot's presentation values are exactly the ones it shipped with.
A regression assertion that the Restaurant's customer path contains no branch on subject id, and that with zero eligible creations customer creation is the human path it is today.

behavioralAcceptance.note: The controller paints several different subjects in Coloring, enters the Restaurant and judges how each one enters, seats, turns and reads at the table. Do not attempt a browser run and do not claim one.
